title: [P0] Account deletion (App Store 5.1.1(v))

- Hard-delete: User node + tokens + push subs + media uploads

- Cascade revocation of any OAuth grants

- After: cannot sign back in with same email (or: re-signup creates a new fresh account)

title: [EPIC] Ambient agents in every chat + bot data-access/privacy model
description:
VISION (Jacob 2026-06-04): an AI agent implicitly present in every chat (yours + others'); bots present in group chats; ability to message someone's bot explicitly; your assistant can cause another's bot to kick something off. Open question: per-user agents ('Jacob's agent' + the other person's agent) vs ONE general useful agent with skills (e.g. NVC mediation as a built-in skill). 

THE CRUX = bot DATA ACCESS / PRIVACY. Must not add your bot to a group and leak personal data. Reference models to mirror: Cortex (total isolation), Noos (private/public/group node visibility), WikiHub (public/public-edit/private/unlisted + teams/grants), Notestream (groups), Collura (?). Idea: tiered access control (private / group-or-team-scoped / public); the agent's data access = union of what the CURRENT context is allowed to see (group chat → only group+public, never your private); approval workflow for the bot to use/send private data; separate scoped memory per bot/context.

MINIMAL DEMO ('poor man's version'): apply the same visibility model (public / group / private) to the OpenChat Thoughtstream THOUGHTS already in-app — a small, concrete demonstration of the access-control behavior.

This epic is DESIGN-FIRST: research prior art across Jacob's projects, then a written design (data model, access-control rules, agent-context scoping, messaging-a-bot UX, NVC-skill plugin model, approval workflow), then phased build starting with the Thoughts-visibility demo.

title: Idempotent message send (client-gen id) + user-room delivery — fixes from Codex review of openchat-5q1
description: Codex review of openchat-5q1 found a regression: the new 10s WS ack timeout + REST fallback can persist the SAME message twice with different server nanoids (WS persists row A, ack lost, REST persists row B). Fix with a client-generated message id used by BOTH paths + server MERGE (create-if-absent). Also: (2) broadcast message:new to each participant's user:<id> room so recipients who haven't joined the conversation room still get it live; (3) dedupe the manual setMessages append in ChatContext catch; (4) add an AbortController timeout to the REST send so the hard-failure path can't hang on mobile/VPN.

title: Mobile/China-VPN users can't send: websocket-only transport + no send queue
description: Lucy (mobile, China VPN) cannot send messages. Root cause: client pins Socket.IO to transports:['websocket'] (no polling fallback) and sendMessage rejects with 'Not connected' the instant the socket is down — no queue/retry. Mobile backgrounding + VPN/GFW reset the WS constantly, so sends land in the disconnected gap and silently drop. Fix: (1) queue-and-retry sends, (2) re-enable polling fallback with WS upgrade, (3) reconnect on visibilitychange. Preserve OpenChat-0kv Cloudflare WS fix.
notes: Root causes: (1) REST POST /conversations/:id/messages never emitted message:new, so socket-down sends (mobile/China VPN) were invisible to recipients. (2) message:send ack had no timeout -> on mobile the Promise hung forever and the REST fallback never fired. Fixed both + MessageInput restores text/toasts on hard failure + useChatSocket reconnects on visibilitychange/online/focus. Transport left websocket-only to preserve OpenChat-0kv. Builds clean. Commit 4908c0b.

title: [P1] Self-serve agent API keys — seamless 'connect your bot' onboarding
description:
Make it dead simple for anyone (Jacob, a user, a friend) to plug their own agent/bot into OpenChat. Today picortex uses a one-off out-of-band JWT minted by a developer. We need a self-serve API key flow with re-viewable keys (NOT one-time-view), provenance fields, scopes, and a working MCP surface.

GOOD PRACTICES TO INHERIT FROM world-issue-tracker + wikihub:

1. **Prefix convention**: keys start with 'oc_' (parallels 'wh_' / 'wit_'). First 12 chars are the visible 'key prefix' used for UI display, full key only visible when retrieved.
2. **Standard Bearer auth**: 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' on every endpoint, not a custom X-Agent-Key header. Matches WikiHub convention (cleaner than WIT's X-Agent-Key).
3. **Provenance fields**: each key has agent_name (e.g. 'my-summary-bot') + agent_version + scopes + expires_at + last_used_at — same shape as WikiHub's ApiKey model.
4. **Scopes**: at minimum 'read' + 'write'. Future: per-conversation scoping, send-only, read-only mention listening.
5. **Credentials file convention**: agents should expect to read from ~/.openchat/credentials.json (mode 0600), parallel to ~/.wikihub/credentials.json.
6. **MCP server**: build a sibling openchat-mcp-server adapter (parallel to wikihub's mcp-server/). Tools: oc_send_message, oc_list_conversations, oc_get_messages, oc_react, oc_create_dm, oc_register_agent. Exposes both stdio + HTTP transports.

DEVIATIONS FROM WIT/WikiHub (per Jacob's explicit feedback):

7. **Keys are RE-VIEWABLE, not one-time-view**. WIT + WikiHub both show the key once at creation and store only the hash — Jacob explicitly does NOT want that. Implementation: store the FULL plaintext key in DB, encrypted at rest with a server-side KMS key (OC_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET env var, rotatable separately from the database). User can re-view any of their keys from Settings → Agent Keys at any time. Threat model: DB read leaks encryption-key-encrypted blob, not plaintext.

UI:
- Settings → Agent Keys (new section)
- List existing keys: name, prefix (oc_xxxx…), last used, expiry, [View] [Revoke] buttons
- 'New key' button: prompts for name + scopes + optional expiry → returns the full key, copy-to-clipboard
- Each key row has [View full key] → reveals plaintext after Face ID / passphrase re-auth (TBD)
- Each key row has [Copy] for the agent name + key in one shot

SERVER:
- New Neo4j node: :AgentKey { id, ownerUserId, name, keyPrefix, keyEncrypted, scopes, agentName, agentVersion, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt }
- (User)-[:OWNS_KEY]->(AgentKey)
- POST /api/agent-keys { name, scopes?, expiresAt? } — authed; mints + returns plaintext
- GET /api/agent-keys — authed; lists keys with prefix-only (no plaintext)
- GET /api/agent-keys/:id/reveal — authed; returns full plaintext key (with audit log entry)
- PATCH /api/agent-keys/:id { name?, scopes? } — authed; rename or change scope
- DELETE /api/agent-keys/:id — authed; sets revokedAt
- New middleware resolveActor: tries JWT first, then Bearer oc_… key. Resolves to owning user. Updates lastUsedAt async.
- Picortex's JWT-based auth stays (don't break) but is grandfathered; future bots go through this.

DOCS:
- README section: 'Connect your bot in 30 seconds'
  1. Settings → Agent Keys → Create
  2. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' https://chat.globalbr.ai/api/chat/conversations
- openchat-mcp-server README + Cursor/Claude Desktop config snippet
- Add to landing page /about: a 'Connect your bot' link with the 30-second walkthrough

ACCEPTANCE:
- A non-technical user can sign up, get an API key, and POST a message via curl in under 2 minutes
- An MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop) can be configured with one JSON snippet to talk to OpenChat
- Keys are re-viewable from Settings indefinitely (until revoked)
- Revocation is immediate (cached resolver invalidated within 60s)
- Audit log of key reveal events

- Programmatic scrollToEnd() should still update isAtBottom correctly via onScroll
- Day separators jump contentSize between messages; use onContentSizeChange to recompute isAtBottom after content grows

title: 401 cascade: app shows error toast then strands user, no logout/refresh path
description:
When the access token expires (15min from Noos), the SPA at chat.globalbr.ai is left in a broken state:

Repro (verified live with Chrome DevTools 2026-05-30, screenshots in /tmp/openchat-04-toast-broken-no-dismiss.png):
1. Token in localStorage.openchat_token expires
2. GET /api/chat/conversations returns 401
3. ApiClient.fetch (client/src/api.ts) throws 'Invalid or expired token' — no refresh attempt, no localStorage clear, no logout, no redirect
4. ChatContext.loadConversations catch shows toast.error('Failed to load conversations') — auto-dismisses after 6s, no X button, no way to dismiss manually
5. Socket.IO useChatSocket connect_error fires with server-side Error('Invalid token') — only console.errors, perpetual 'Reconnecting...' spinner

Fix work is in git stash@{0}: 'stash-during-darkmode-deploy' — 6 files, ~455 insertions, codex-reviewed shape + implementation. Includes:
- Single-flight refresh via shared promise (Noos refresh tokens are rotated — would race otherwise)
- New refreshAccessToken() / clearAuth() / emitTokenRefreshed / emitAuthExpired helpers in api.ts
- 401-then-refresh-then-retry in fetch<T>() and getMe() (also fixes latent /me URL bug — was hitting /api/chat/me instead of /api/auth/me)
- Refresh-loop guard: consecutiveRefreshes counter capped at REFRESH_LOOP_LIMIT=3 (codex 2026-05-30 caught the per-effect-run flag would loop forever if every refreshed token is rejected)
- ChatProvider listens for noos:token-refreshed (updates React token state) + noos:auth-expired (clears state + navigate('/login') + toast)
- New utils/toastError.tsx component: dismissible (X button + click-anywhere + Esc), role=alert, aria-live=assertive, stable-id de-dupe (so loadConversations spam doesn't stack)
- All 10 toast.error() sites swapped to toastError() with stable IDs
- logout() now clears openchat_refresh_token (was leaking)
- register/ssoExchange now persist refreshToken (was dropping it)

Codex critique status: blessed shape + impl after addressing the refresh-loop guard. Remaining concerns are non-blocking (SSR guards in ChatProvider, possible slight double-toast on auth-expired).

title: [Bug] First message to picortex bot on a brand-new DM gets no reply (discovery race)
description:
Symptom (Jacob, 2026-04-23): DMing picortex@bot.globalbr.ai on chat.globalbr.ai for the first time, the bot does NOT reply. The SECOND message reliably gets a reply. Jacob suspected a timing issue.

Root cause: CONFIRMED — conversation-discovery race.

Evidence (replicated 2026-04-24 03:37-03:38 UTC):
- Fresh test user e2e_fresh_1777001825 creates NEW DM with bot via POST /api/chat/conversations (participantIds=['picortex_bot_...'], type='direct'). Convo id: bFh8_dWEIXwNvNEH3hwJF.
- Tester immediately sends 'FIRST msg' (message id qXVCMaK2THy3zKYZMPtUT). Broadcast via io.to('conversation:bFh8...').emit('message:new', ...). Bot is NOT in that room yet → not delivered.
- ~2s later picortex's 30s poll fires (03:37:47), sees the new convo (total 3→4), emits conversation:join, enters the room.
- Tester sends 'SECOND msg' at 03:38:00 (id 3uUODTcqrOLrrFa3cpdUb). Bot receives it and replies 2s later with 'Hey! Got your message. What can I help you with?'.
- picortex journalctl confirms: the first message id NEVER appears in logs; the second message id does. Bot-side socket only received the convo it just joined.

Root cause in code
- server/src/websocket/chatHandler.ts message:send handler (line 148): io.to('conversation:' + conversationId).emit('message:new', message). Only sockets that have previously called conversation:join are in the room.
- server/src/routes/chat.ts POST /conversations (lines 66-138): creates Conversation + PARTICIPATES_IN edges, returns 201. NO socket emit to notify the other participants that they are now in a new conversation.
- No conversation:created, conversation:new, or participant:added event exists on the socket server.
- Bot-side mitigation is a 30s poll (OpenChat-3ld: 'Periodic re-poll every 30s for newly-added conversations'), which creates a 0-30s window where the first message is silently dropped.

Proposed fix (server side — this ticket)
- In chat.ts POST /conversations: after CREATE, for each participant, io.to(<their user room / sockets>).emit('conversation:created', conversation) — or emit 'participant:added' to each participant.
- Options for addressing sockets per user: (a) have every socket join a 'user:${userId}' room on connect in chatHandler.ts, then emit io.to('user:' + participantId); (b) iterate userSockets map.
- Consider same event for 'add participant to existing conversation' flow (groups) once that UI ships — solves the same race for groups.
- Optionally: also buffer/retry the initial message:send if it finds zero room members who are actual participants — but the proper fix is the event.

Proposed fix (bot side — track via OpenChat-3ld)
- picortex listens for conversation:created / participant:added; on receipt, immediately GET conversation and emit conversation:join before any message arrives.
- Keep the 30s poll as a fallback.

Repro script
- /Users/Jacob/code/picortex/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8b9f846/scripts/e2e-openchat-new-convo.mjs
- Env: OPENCHAT_JWT_SECRET, TESTER_USER_ID, TESTER_EMAIL, BOT_USER_ID (default picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef). Use a FRESH tester user that has no prior conversation with the bot (create in Neo4j first).
- Verdict field 'hypothesis_confirmed' prints true when first msg gets no reply and second msg does.

Related tickets
- OpenChat-3ld (picortex OpenChatChannel impl; v0.2 bullet listens for conversation:added — this is that event, needs server side)
- OpenChat-aoy (Group chats validation — same race affects adding bot to existing group)
- OpenChat-8bk (picortex bot user flow)
- OpenChat-qz0 (Add connection recovery for missed messages — related but not the same issue)

title: Real-time sidebar updates and unread message indicators
description:
**Problem:**
Two related issues with message notifications and real-time updates:

1. **Sidebar doesn't update for non-active conversations**
   - When you have conversation A open and receive a message in conversation B, the sidebar doesn't show that B has new messages
   - No unread badge/indicator appears
   - Conversation order doesn't update to show most recent at top
   - Have to click on the conversation to see there's a new message

2. **New contact messages require page refresh**
   - When someone new messages you, it doesn't appear in the conversation list
   - Must refresh the entire page to see the new conversation

**What's idiomatic in chat apps (Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Messenger):**

1. **Unread indicators:**
   - Red dot/badge with unread count on conversations
   - Bold text for conversation name when unread
   - Preview text shows latest message

2. **Conversation list behavior:**
   - Conversations reorder in real-time (most recent at top)
   - New conversations appear automatically at top
   - Visual highlight/animation when new message arrives

3. **Real-time updates via WebSocket:**
   - Already have WebSocket for messages in active chat
   - Need to also push updates to sidebar state
   - When message received for conversation X: update X's lastMessage, lastMessageAt, unreadCount

**Implementation approach:**

1. **State management:**
   - Track unreadCount per conversation
   - Update when: message received for non-active conversation
   - Clear when: user opens that conversation

2. **WebSocket events:**
   - On new_message event: update the affected conversation in sidebar state
   - On new_conversation event: add to conversation list

3. **UI components:**
   - Add unread badge component to ConversationListItem
   - Sort conversations by lastMessageAt (descending)
   - Highlight/animate on new message

**Affects:** Core chat UX - users expect real-time updates in any modern chat app
close_reason: v1 shipped (45f9b80). Client-side unreadByConv Map in ChatContext, bumped in handleMessage when conv is non-active and sender isn't self, cleared in setActiveConversation. ConversationList renders a blue pill (99+ cap) + bolder weight for unread rows. Real-time sidebar reorder was already in place from the 401-cascade work (handleMessage re-sorts conversations on every inbound). v2 — server-side lastReadAt + cross-device sync — left as follow-up, not blocking. Stretch animation/highlight per ticket also deferred.

title: Secure SSO token exchange (don't pass JWT in URL)
description:
SECURITY: Passing JWTs in URL query parameters is a security risk.

**Current:** GET /auth/callback?token=jwt_here
URLs are logged in browser history, proxy logs, server access logs.

**Fix options:**
1. Use fragment identifier (#token=...) - not sent to server
2. Use short-lived exchange code (OAuth2 pattern) - POST to exchange for JWT
3. Use HttpOnly cookies for session management

From Gemini audit: 'Passing JWTs in URL query parameters is a security risk'

title: [decision] Agent heartbeat → outbound notifications to hooks: native vs external personal agent
description:
A periodic 'heartbeat' where the agent proactively reviews state (important new messages, triage results, reminders, things needing attention) and pushes notifications OUT to hooks — webhooks, push, Slack, the user's other channels.

KEY DECISION (the reason this is a [decision] ticket): implement natively in OpenChat vs rely on the user's EXTERNAL personal agent.
- NATIVE: server-side per-user scheduler + webhook/notification dispatch. Works for everyone out-of-box; we own the scheduler + inference cost + reliability.
- EXTERNAL: the user's own personal agent polls OpenChat's API on its schedule and decides what to notify (fits the Shipper 'your app is a tool the agent calls' thesis). More personalized + offloads cost, but only works for users who HAVE a personal agent.

RECOMMENDATION TO EVALUATE: do BOTH — expose the API/event surface (a webhook/events feed + 'what needs attention' endpoint) so external agents can drive it, AND ship a lightweight native heartbeat for users without a personal agent. Depends on the access-control model (openchat-j0o) and the triage feature (bfn inbound-triage). Decide before building.

Reuses the Assistant runtime + tools (bfn.3) but as a docked overlay surface that knows where you are (active conversationId, selection) and can act (summarize this thread, draft a reply, search related, file feedback, triage). title: Inbound triage: classify new senders as relationship-worthy vs spam (a 'Requests'/'Filtered' inbox)

An agent that processes INBOUND messages — especially from unknown/new senders — and classifies whether this is someone you'd want to relate with vs spam/unwanted, routing accordingly. Like iMessage 'Unknown Senders' / Instagram 'Message Requests', but agent-driven.

Signals to combine: sender reputation/history, whether they're in your contacts or share a group, message content (LLM classification — outreach vs spam vs scam), your public profile/interests, and (later) the shared social graph. Output: route to Primary inbox vs a Requests queue vs Spam; optionally let your agent draft a reply, summarize the request, or auto-decline.

Surfaces: a Requests/Filtered view in the conversation list (web + mobile). Respect the access-control model (openchat-j0o) — the agent only sees what the context allows. Ties to the contacts/people directory (openchat-2rn) and the assistant runtime (bfn.3).

title: Forward-to-my-agent: long-press any message in any chat to privately send it to my Assistant
description:
Idea (Jacob 2026-06-04): from EVERY conversation at all times, let me tag/forward a specific message to my own Assistant agent privately — e.g. long-press a message → 'Ask my agent' / 'Forward to Assistant' → it lands in my private Assistant DM (only I see it) with the original message as context, so I can ask the agent to act on it (summarize, draft a reply, remember it, file feedback, search related, etc.) without the other participants knowing.

Design considerations to weigh:
- ENTRY POINT: message action menu (long-press mobile / hover menu web) item 'Ask my agent' or 'Forward to Assistant'. Possibly also an always-present affordance (a persistent '@agent' you can tag inline in any message — but inline @agent in a shared convo risks leaking to others, so the long-press→private-forward path is the privacy-safe default).
- PRIVACY: the forward must go to the user's OWN Assistant DM (containsBot self-conversation), NOT post into the shared conversation. The other participants must never see it. Carry a reference {sourceConversationId, sourceMessageId, quoted content} so the Assistant has context.
- TWO MODES likely: (a) 'Forward to Assistant' (just drops the message into the Assistant DM as quoted context), (b) 'Ask my agent about this' (forwards + prompts for a question). 
- INLINE @agent (stretch): typing @agent / #agent in a shared message could trigger the bot to reply — but only privately to the tagger, or visibly to all? Decide. Inline-visible @agent = a shared AI helper (different product surface). Keep separate from the private forward.
- Reuse: builds on the Assistant bot (openchat-bfn.3) + its tools; the forward is essentially 'create/append to the self Assistant DM with a quoted message + optional FROM_MESSAGE link for provenance'.
- Parity: implement in apps/mobile (long-press) AND apps/web (hover menu). Backend: a small endpoint POST /api/assistant/forward { sourceConversationId, sourceMessageId, question? } that injects the quoted context into the user's Assistant DM and triggers a turn.

Relates to: openchat-bfn (assistant epic), openchat-bfn.4 (guardrails).

title: Make local-build.sh self-heal Node version (don't rely on machine-local .xcode.env.local)
description:
TestFlight build failed twice with 'Unable to resolve module index.ts' because the Xcode 'Bundle React Native code and images' phase ran under Node 25 (brew auto-bumped the unversioned node keg). Expo SDK 54/RN 0.81/Metro need Node 20/22/24.

Key gotcha: the Xcode build phase sources ios/.xcode.env which does NODE_BINARY=$(command -v node) in a PATH-sanitized shell — so prepending node@22 to PATH in the launching shell does NOT reach the phase. Fix that worked: ios/.xcode.env.local with 'export NODE_BINARY=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin/node'. But that file is machine-local + gitignored, so other machines/agents will hit this again.

Durable fix options (pick one):
1. local-build.sh detects $(node -v) major not in {20,22,24} and writes ios/.xcode.env.local pinning to an installed LTS (brew --prefix node@22) before building.
2. Commit a versioned .xcode.env that prefers node@22 if present.
3. Add an engines/Volta pin + docs.
Recommend option 1 (self-healing script). Also pinned repo via .node-version=22 (committed) — but Xcode's NODE_BINARY ignores .node-version, hence the script guard.
notes: TRUE root cause of headless build failure is NOT node — it's TMPDIR. Claude Code's TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501 causes a /tmp vs /private/tmp symlink mismatch that breaks Metro's absolute --entry-file resolution. Durable fix for local-build.sh: at the top, if TMPDIR resolves under /tmp, re-point it to a canonical /private/tmp dir (mkdir -p /private/tmp/ocbuild; export TMPDIR=/private/tmp/ocbuild). Combine with the node@22 LTS guard. Then headless/agent (nohup) builds work without NoMachine.
close_reason: Added TMPDIR + Node self-heal guards to local-build.sh (openchat-mobile commit). TMPDIR repin to $HOME/.ocbuild-tmp was the real fix (avoids /tmp<->/private/tmp Metro resolution bug); Node-LTS PATH guard as secondary. Headless nohup build now archives + submits to TestFlight without NoMachine. Verified v0.1.14 build 71.

title: register() and ssoExchange() drop refreshToken from the return — session is non-refreshable from birth
description:
client/src/api.ts:240-269 (register) and 293-324 (ssoExchange) destructure { accessToken, user } from the Noos response and don't include refreshToken. Caller in ChatContext.noosRegister / ssoLogin can't persist it, so localStorage.openchat_refresh_token is never set for those auth paths.

Consequence: users who registered via Noos OR signed in via SSO (the 'Continue with Noos' button on chat.globalbr.ai) get a session that can never refresh. Their first 401 → can't refresh → forced logout. Only password-login users currently get refresh.

Fix: in stash@{0} — both methods return { token, refreshToken, user } and the ChatContext call sites localStorage.setItem('openchat_refresh_token', result.refreshToken). Could be cherry-picked from the bigger 401 fix.
close_reason: Shipped in eff5ca1 — 401 cascade fix from stash@{2} re-applied on top of Google OAuth merge, conflicts resolved, build clean. Includes single-flight refresh, refresh-loop guard, refreshToken persistence in register/ssoExchange (-bo6), getMe URL fix (-924), trust-proxy for express (-9jm), dismissible toast helper. Google OAuth smoke test 13/13 still green.

title: [UX] Dark mode for OpenChat web app
description:
Add proper dark mode to OpenChat's web client. The app is currently bg-white / text-gray-900 across all surfaces — fine in daylight, harsh at night, and obviously not parity with the iMessage / WhatsApp / Telegram default that users expect.

## Approach
- Enable Tailwind dark mode: 'class' strategy in tailwind.config.js (not 'media' — we want user override, not system-only).
- Toggle in user menu (ChatSidebar's user dropdown): Light / Dark / System. Default 'System'.
- Persist choice in localStorage 'openchat_theme'. On boot, main.tsx applies the saved/derived class to <html>.
- React to system pref changes (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener) when in System mode.
- Update the existing <meta name='theme-color'> from #3b82f6 to also have a dark variant (use media-attribute form: <meta name='theme-color' content='#1e293b' media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'>) so the iOS Safari URL-bar tints correctly.
- Update manifest.webmanifest theme_color + background_color to have light/dark counterparts where browsers support it (only some do; safe to keep current light defaults).

## Files to audit for hardcoded colors
Every component that currently uses bg-white / bg-gray-50 / text-gray-* / border-gray-* needs dark: variants. Inventory from grep:
- client/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx (bg-gray-50 outer, header bg-white)
- client/src/components/ChatSidebar.tsx (bg-white, gray borders, status dropdown)
- client/src/components/ConversationList.tsx
- client/src/components/MessageList.tsx (bg-blue-500 own bubbles -> stays; bg-gray-100 other bubbles -> dark:bg-gray-700; text-gray-900 -> dark:text-gray-100)
- client/src/components/MessageInput.tsx (bg-white form, border-gray-200, border-gray-300 input)
- client/src/components/GroupSettings.tsx (modal bg-white)
- client/src/components/PresenceIndicator.tsx (presence dot colors — likely keep)
- client/src/components/InstallPrompt.tsx (sheet bg-white)
- client/src/App.tsx Toaster (already uses bg-red-100 / bg-green-100 — those work in both modes but darker variants would be cleaner)
- client/src/index.css base body bg
- The Noos feedback widget is 3rd-party; can't directly themed. data-theme='auto' is already set in index.html so it should respect prefers-color-scheme automatically.

## UX details
- Switch should be near-instant (no flash of unstyled content). Apply theme class BEFORE React mounts — in a small inline <script> in index.html that reads localStorage and applies the class to <html> synchronously.
- Bubble color choice for dark mode: own messages stay blue, others go to dark-gray (e.g. bg-slate-700). Sender-name labels go to slate-400.
- Status indicators (green/yellow/red/gray dots) stay the same vivid colors in both modes.
- Floating Noos widget data-theme='auto' should pick up the change.

## Acceptance
- Toggle in user menu works (Light / Dark / System).
- System mode tracks OS preference live (no reload needed).
- No flash of light theme on dark-mode-saved cold load.
- All conversation surfaces (list / chat / group settings modal / install prompt / login) look polished in dark.
- iOS Safari URL-bar tints with the theme.

## Phase
Phase 1 polish — chunky-but-not-blocking. Ship before declaring mobile UX 'done.' Roughly half a day of careful component-by-component audit + a couple of hours for the theme toggle infrastructure.

title: [Group chats] Validate picortex bot works in group conversations end-to-end
description:
Sibling of picortex-hal (P2, picortex-side group-chat validation pass). Today picortex is only tested/used in DMs (type: 'direct') on chat.globalbr.ai. The bot auto-joins any conversation it's a participant in via polling GET /api/chat/conversations, but OpenChat may have different routing semantics for group vs direct conversations and there is no 'add bot to group' flow.

Scope
- Verify end-to-end: bot added as participant in a type='group' Conversation, message:new fires for bot on group messages, bot's message:send via socket broadcasts correctly to all group participants.
- Audit server/src/routes/chat.ts and server/src/websocket/chatHandler.ts for any branch that treats type='group' differently from type='direct' (permission checks, room membership, deduplication, etc.).
- Test scenarios: (a) bot in group from creation, (b) bot added to existing group after creation, (c) bot removed from group, (d) multiple humans + bot in same group, (e) bot-only messages vs human-to-human messages (discriminate/mention-only behavior).

Likely implementation gaps
- UI: no 'add bot to group' flow in the OpenChat web client (see OpenChat-88z new-conversation contact picker for nearby UX).
- Server: no participant:added socket event emitted when a user is added to an existing conversation — bot would miss it until next 30s poll (same race as the first-message bug, see sibling ticket 'First message to picortex gets no reply').
- Server: no discrimination between 'bot should reply to every message in DM' vs 'bot should only reply when mentioned/addressed in group'. Add per-conversation bot-behavior flags (quiet mode, mention-only).

Dependencies
- Blocked-by / related-to: sibling bug ticket 'First message to picortex gets no reply' — same discovery race affects newly-added participants in groups.
- Related: picortex-hal (picortex-side validation pass, P2, filed earlier today)
- Related: OpenChat-3ld (picortex OpenChatChannel impl) — v0.2 bullet already lists 'listen for conversation:added event'; that event should also cover participant:added for groups.
- Related: OpenChat-8bk (picortex bot user flow)

Acceptance
- Green e2e: human creates group with bot, sends message, bot receives and replies. Same again after bot is added mid-conversation.
- Documented bot-behavior defaults for groups (mention-only by default is reasonable).
- Any server changes land behind feature flag until picortex-hal ships the matching client-side support.
close_reason: Shipped. Server already emits participant:added / conversation:created (confirmed). picortex now LISTENS for them (patched openchat.ts on the VM — auto-joins on add, drops on remove) AND routes outbound through the originating channel (fixed dispatcher.ts where every reply was being silently sent through Linq instead of OpenChat — the actual cause of 'first message gets no reply'). Verified end-to-end via Chrome bridge: tmad4000 sent 'Reply test 2 — say pong', picortex replied 'pong' within seconds. OpenChat web client also renders BotBadge for isBot users in contact picker, sidebar, conversation header, and group settings. Picortex source snapshots saved to /Users/Jacob/code/picortex/deployed-snapshots/2026-05-30-agent-chat-fix/.

title: Sync SSO flow with Thoughtstreams / latest Noos pattern
description:
OpenChat SSO diverges from Thoughtstreams:

1. Thoughtstreams proxies /api/auth/sso-exchange through its own server; OpenChat calls Noos directly from the browser (cross-origin, requires CORS, leaks Noos URL, bakes in VITE_NOOS_URL at build time). Refactor OpenChat to POST to /api/auth/sso-exchange on its own server and have the server talk to Noos internally via NOOS_API_URL (already in docker-compose). Benefits: no cross-origin fetch, no VITE_NOOS_URL dependency for the exchange path, matches Thoughtstreams.

2. Thoughtstreams calls /auth/session-check on load to auto-resume a Noos session. OpenChat does not — users must click Continue with Noos even if already signed in on ts.globalbr.ai. Add session-check for true cross-app SSO.

3. Consider extracting a shared noos-sso npm module (used by OpenChat, Thoughtstreams, thoughtstream-gemini-jacob) so auth drift stops happening per-app. Tracked under noos-sso-ecosystem epic.

title: Decision: phone-number sign-in (WhatsApp-style)?
description:
DECISION ticket, not implementation. Decide whether/when to add SMS-OTP sign-in alongside Google OAuth.

CURRENT STATE: Google OAuth only (iOS + web). No phoneNumber field on :User. ~5 users.

TRADEOFF MATRIX:
| Dim                       | Google (today) | Phone+OTP                | Both                |
|---------------------------|----------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| Onboarding friction       | Medium         | Low                      | Low                 |
| Cost                      | $0            | $0.005-0.04/SMS         | Marginal            |
| Dev/test                  | Easy           | Hard                     | Hard                |
| Abuse surface             | Low            | SIM swap, toll fraud     | Both                |
| Contacts matching         | Useless        | High value               | High value          |
| Portability               | Stable         | Numbers recycle          | Both                |
| iOS App Store             | Fine           | Triggers SIWA req        | SIWA req            |
| Time-to-ship              | N/A            | 1-2 weeks                | Same                |

RECOMMENDATION: DEFER. Stay Google-only for ~3 months. Revisit triggers:
  (a) >100 users AND contacts-matching is top growth lever, OR
  (b) Specific repeat user blocked by no-Google option.

WHEN BUILT: use Twilio Verify (not raw Programmable SMS) + add Sign in with Apple simultaneously (App Store rule). Design account-merge UX BEFORE first SMS goes out.

DO-NOW PREP (low effort, future-proofs):
- [ ] Add nullable phoneNumber (E.164) + phoneNumberVerifiedAt fields to :User in Neo4j (no migration needed)
- [ ] Add phoneNumberHash (sha256(E.164)) index

ACCEPTANCE:

  (b) move to codex's two-axis homeScope+visibility model

Decide schema approach when this becomes urgent. Defer until then (v1 doesn't need it).

title: getMe() hits /api/chat/me instead of /api/auth/me (URL bug)
description:
client/src/api.ts:273 calls this.fetch('/me'.replace('/chat', '/auth'))) — but path is just '/me' (replace matches nothing), then fetch prepends API_BASE = '/api/chat', so the actual request goes to /api/chat/me (which 404s).

Symptom: getMe() always fails. Probably masked because the call sites have fallbacks or aren't hit on most flows.

Fix: in stash@{0}, getMe() uses `/me` directly with its own auth headers + 401-retry logic. Could be cherry-picked out of the bigger 401 work if you want to fix it independently.

title: [Mobile] Dark mode for the React Native app (when it lands)
description:
When the React Native prototype (OpenChat-dv0) becomes a real shipping app, it needs dark mode parity with the web app.

## Approach
- React Native: useColorScheme() from 'react-native' (Appearance API) gives system preference live.
- Theme provider context (or just a useThemed hook) exposing semantic tokens (background, surface, primary, textPrimary, textSecondary, divider, bubbleOwn, bubbleOther, bubbleOwnText, bubbleOtherText, etc.).
- Persist user override (Light / Dark / System) via AsyncStorage / MMKV.
- All shared design tokens should match the web app's dark palette one-to-one so cross-platform users see the same colors.
- Native side benefits the web app can't easily get:
  - Status bar style (light/dark content) via StatusBar component.
  - iOS navigation bar tint (UIBarStyle / scheme on the wrapper).
  - Apple's smart-invert handled by the system.
  - Native blur effects on dark surfaces (BlurView) where appropriate.

## Cross-platform consistency
- Pick the design tokens BEFORE writing the web dark mode (OpenChat-?? sibling ticket). Web and RN should share a single color spec, not diverge.
- Document the spec in a single ~/code/openchat/docs/theme.md or similar.
- If we later add a Capacitor or full-RN shell, the same tokens apply.

## Phase
Phase 2 — does NOT need to land until the RN prototype itself does (OpenChat-dv0). Filed now so it's not forgotten when the RN work begins.

Depends on OpenChat-dv0 (RN prototype) + the web dark mode sibling ticket for the source-of-truth color spec.
